sections.html: Syracuse, the county seat, is the single city in Onondaga County. The rest is towns, villages and hamlets, and where your parcel sits decides which office collects your tax. The county has an estimated 466,584 people and 212,925 housing units, with 65.9% of homes owner-occupied. The median owner-occupied home is worth $200,200 and median gross rent is $1,108, so a tax balance of a few thousand dollars takes a real bite out of a typical sale.

sections.h2: Who sends and collects property tax bills in Onondaga County?
sections.html:
County Finance prepares the bills for the county, town, school and village levies, and it collects the delinquent amounts on all four. Its Real Property Tax Services office sits on the 15th floor of the Civic Center at 421 Montgomery Street in Syracuse, and the number on the county pages is 315-435-2426.

Delinquent payments for parcels outside the City of Syracuse go to that office. Syracuse city parcels are handled on the city side, so a seller with a Syracuse address should ask the city about a payoff instead of calling the county.

  • Pay online, view bills and print receipts for town properties through the RPTS pages.
  • Mail a check made out to Chief Fiscal Officer, PO Box 1004, Syracuse, NY 13201.
  • Pull up sales history, lot dimensions and assessed values through the county's parcel lookup.
  • Tax maps can be ordered online, at the office or by mail.

The county treats each kind of bill as delinquent after a set date. If your school or village bill from this year is still open, it is already in the delinquent column.

Delinquency dates used by the county
Tax typeDelinquent if unpaid by
County taxMarch 31 of its year
School taxNovember 1
Village taxNovember 1

An owner can redeem a delinquent lien by paying the enforcing officer before the redemption period runs out. Unless the tax district sets something else, that is two years from the lien date (Real Property Tax Law section 1110). Counties can stretch it for homes and farms or cut it for vacant and abandoned houses, so get the actual lien date from the county before counting on two full years.

A payoff for a single parcel comes only from the RPTS office, so request a written figure that is good through your planned closing day. Interest keeps adding while the bill is open, which is why a quote from a few weeks earlier can be wrong.

The county runs its real property tax auction once a year, in October, on an online platform, and it begins listing the parcels in September. Those parcels come from the county's collection of unpaid taxes, which is why the RPTS office is the right first call for an owner who is behind.

If your parcel could be on the list, call RPTS now and ask how far along it is. Put the answer in writing. Then weigh the payoff against what a sale would bring before choosing to pay, sell or wait.

sections.h2: How do I contest an assessment or claim an exemption?
sections.html:
Assessments are set town by town, with county staff supporting the assessors on tax law and maps. Complaint hearings before the board of assessment review start on the fourth Tuesday of May unless a local law picks another day (Real Property Tax Law section 512). Check the date with your town assessor in spring.

When the board refuses a reduction you have two routes. Small Claims Assessment Review costs less and is open to most homeowners. A tax certiorari case in State Supreme Court is the heavier option, and a lawyer is advised. Either way, the local grievance comes first.

The county RPTS page gives March 1 as the exemption deadline for county properties outside the city of Syracuse. If you are about to sell, the STAR credit is the exemption most owners ask about. Cancel your registration with the State Tax Department at the sale. The new owner registers on their own.

sections.h2: Selling a house when tax is still owed
sections.html:
First work out who holds the balance: RPTS outside Syracuse, the city's own tax office inside it. Request a payoff letter showing tax, interest and added fees, and hand it to your closing attorney.

  • Find out if a delinquent lien is on file and when it attached.
  • Check whether any school or village balance has been moved onto the next county bill.
  • Ask whether the parcel appears on the auction listings that begin in September.
  • Pick a closing date well before any redemption deadline.

A cash buyer can take the house as it stands, tax debt, repairs and tenants included, which spares you the work of getting it ready for a financed buyer. Weigh that against listing with an agent, and keep the redemption date in view either way.

sections.h2: Order of calls before you list
sections.html:
Working through these steps in order keeps a tax problem from surfacing in the middle of a contract.

  1. Look up the parcel in the county's lookup to confirm the assessed value, lot dimensions and sales history match what you expect.
  2. Call RPTS at 315-435-2426 (or the city if the house is in Syracuse) and ask whether any school, village, town or county balance is open.
  3. Ask for the lien date, if there is one, and note which redemption period applies.
  4. Get the payoff in writing and send it to your closing attorney together with your most recent bills.
  5. If a STAR registration exists, plan to close it at the sale. Your buyer registers separately.
  6. Ask the town assessor whether an exemption you hold ends with the sale, and whether any grievance you filed is still pending.

Tax follows the land, not the seller. A balance you ignore will not vanish at the closing table: it is paid from your proceeds or it stays with the house. Learning the number early lets you set the sale up on your own terms. It also lets you compare a listing, which has its own timeline and showings, against a quicker cash sale where the buyer takes on the house and its liens as they stand.

faqs.q: Who do I pay if my Onondaga County property tax is late?
faqs.a: For parcels outside Syracuse, pay Real Property Tax Services at the Civic Center, 15th floor, or mail a check to Chief Fiscal Officer, PO Box 1004, Syracuse, NY 13201. The number is 315-435-2426. City parcels go through the city.

faqs.q: What dates make an Onondaga County tax delinquent?
faqs.a: A county tax not paid by March 31 and a school or village tax not paid by November 1 are treated as delinquent by the county. Ask RPTS for the exact total on your parcel.

faqs.q: How long can I redeem a parcel with a delinquent tax lien?
faqs.a: The default redemption period is two years from the lien date under Real Property Tax Law section 1110. A tax district can extend it for residential and farm property or shorten it to one year for vacant and abandoned homes. Ask the county which period applies to your parcel.

faqs.q: When is the Onondaga County tax auction?
faqs.a: The county holds its real property tax auction once a year in October, online, and it starts listing parcels in September. For the current list, use the RPTS auction page, since the parcels change every year.

faqs.q: Can I sell a house in Onondaga County that has a tax lien?
faqs.a: Yes. The lien is paid off as part of the sale, and the payoff figure comes from the county RPTS office or, inside Syracuse, from the city. Get that written figure before you set a closing date, and sell before the redemption period or foreclosure steps remove your right to the house.
